question: Should OpenClaw ship a supported, operator-accessible Telegram direct-message recovery feature, or should this experimental recovery lifecycle remain out of the product and public plugin SDK?
rationale: The branch is intentionally disabled and adds a new channel recovery policy plus public SDK contracts; choosing its permanent owner, enablement surface, and compatibility promise requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Sponsor a Telegram-owned feature
options.body: Keep the work in the Telegram plugin, add a supported enablement and persistence owner, and replace Telegram-named SDK exports with a generic delivery contract.

options.title: Defer the recovery feature
options.body: Close or substantially narrow the branch until maintainers choose a product requirement and supported operating model.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a Telegram-owned feature
recommendation.body: Keep the work in the Telegram plugin, add a supported enablement and persistence owner, and replace Telegram-named SDK exports with a generic delivery contract.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a product-boundary and plugin-SDK contract decision rather than a mechanical test repair.
